speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned experiencing persistent vomiting and chest pain; to help me understand the severity and potential cause, have you noticed any radiation of the pain to your arm, jaw, or back, or have you experienced shortness of breath? Also, when did these symptoms first start?

speaker: Patient
text: 51-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with persistent, forceful vomiting after consuming a significant amount of alcohol. His medical history includes recent treatment for Lyme disease with doxycycline. Recently, after a prolonged episode of retching, the patient starts to choke and cough forcefully, experiencing chest pain. The patient appears unable to communicate effectively at this point.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Boerhaave Syndrome (Esophageal Rupture).

The history of forceful vomiting following heavy alcohol consumption, followed by chest pain, choking, and coughing, is highly specific for this condition. Given the severity of symptoms and the risk of mediastinitis, I am proceeding with immediate imaging confirmation.

REQUEST IMAGES: Chest_X-Ray (upright and left lateral decubitus views).
